Q: Embed a base64-encoded image at the bottom of HTML file A:

I <3 the given css solution.

Advantages:

  • You can place the large base64 text at the bottom of the html document.

  • The BASE64 image(s) are defined within the html, not external. Makes transportability easier (similar to pdf).

I guess you can also use:

#MYIMG01 to define the BASE64 image (at the bottom of the document) and reference is with id="MYIMG01" in the img tag. And so on MYIMG02, 03. Like variables, so to speak.

One of the reasons users might want this html-BASE64 solution is e.g. the fact that pdf's often get bad reflow (line breaks) and too small font size on android devices. So you can make a very nice simple html document with css font-size:large, with some body and,or pre wrapping, probably a viewport meta tag definition at the top and with the images straight in the document. I've checked, the Android html viewer renders the webpage-document with the BASE64 images well. More readable than some pdfs (depending on their layout).

Q: Not able to see black and white image after threshold application A:

In Python OpenCV, you can do color thresholding more easily with cv2.inRange().

Also you should be able to get the left line more easily if you convert to YCbCr colorspace and use the Cb channel. The line will be very dark against a light gray background. The other lines do not show up.

But using the HLS colorspace, you can do the following to extract each line separately. I get some of each line. You can modify the code to try to achieve more of each line and any other line you want.

  • Read the input

  • Convert to HLS colorspace

  • Threshold on the left line in the image using cv2.inRange()

  • Apply morphology close

  • Get the largest contour and draw as white filled on a black background

  • Repeat the same process starting with the thresholding for any other different color line

  • Merge the contours into one image

  • Draw it as red filled on a copy of the input

  • Save the images

Input Image:

import cv2
import numpy as np

# read the input
img = cv2.imread('road_lines.jpg')

# convert to HLS colorspace
hls = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HLS)

# threshold on the left line
low = (20,145,180)
high = (45,155,255)
thresh1 = cv2.inRange(hls, low, high)

# apply morphology
kernel = cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE, (9,9))
morph1 = cv2.morphologyEx(thresh1, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel)

# get largest contour
contours = cv2.findContours(morph1, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
contours = contours[0] if len(contours) == 2 else contours[1]
cntr1 = max(contours, key=cv2.contourArea)

# draw contour as white filled on black background
cntr1_img = np.zeros_like(morph1)
cv2.drawContours(cntr1_img, [cntr1], 0, (255), -1)


# threshold on the next line to the right
low = (10,240,255)
high = (25,250,255)
thresh2 = cv2.inRange(hls, low, high)

# apply morphology
kernel = cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE, (9,9))
morph2 = cv2.morphologyEx(thresh2, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel)

# get largest contour and draw as white filled on black background
contours = cv2.findContours(morph2, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
contours = contours[0] if len(contours) == 2 else contours[1]
cntr2 = max(contours, key=cv2.contourArea)

# draw contour as white filled on black background
cntr2_img = np.zeros_like(morph2)
cv2.drawContours(cntr2_img, [cntr2], 0, (255), -1)

# merge the two contours
cntrs_img = cv2.add(cntr1_img, cntr2_img)

# draw contours as red on copy of input image
result = img.copy()
result[cntrs_img==255] = (0,0,255)

# save the images
cv2.imwrite('road_lines_thresh1.jpg', thresh1)
cv2.imwrite('road_lines_thresh2.jpg', thresh2)
cv2.imwrite('road_lines_morph1.jpg', morph1)
cv2.imwrite('road_lines_morph2.jpg', morph2)
cv2.imwrite('road_lines_contour1.jpg', cntr1_img)
cv2.imwrite('road_lines_contour2.jpg', cntr2_img)
cv2.imwrite('road_lines_both_contours.jpg', cntrs_img)
cv2.imwrite('road_lines_result.jpg', result)

# show the images
cv2.imshow('thresh1', thresh1)
cv2.imshow('thresh2', thresh2)
cv2.imshow('morph1', morph1)
cv2.imshow('morph2', morph2)
cv2.imshow('contour1', cntr1_img)
cv2.imshow('contour2', cntr2_img)
cv2.imshow('both contours', cntrs_img)
cv2.imshow('result', result)
cv2.waitKey(0)

Q: C# Entity Framework "An entity object cannot be referenced by multiple instances of IEntityChangeTracker" A:

there can be several reasons described:

  1. Querying an entity from one DbContext and trying to update it with another - in diferent using-clauses
  • Solution: avoid using multiple contexts for the same entity instances
  1. Trying to attach an entity that is already attached to another context - also when dong it in diferent using-clauses
  • Solution: detach entities if needed when moving them between contexts
  1. Querying related entities with lazy loading in a using block - if after some manipulations with object you try to access related children from Include not yet fixed in .ToArray() or .ToList()
  • Solution: In this scenario, you should avoid using lazy loading (eager load related entities using .Include()) or detach the parent entity before using its related entities outside of the context scope.

you can detach the entity from the previous IEntityChangeTracker instance before adding the related object. You can do this using the DbContext.Entry() method to get the EntityEntry for the entity, and then calling the EntityEntry.State property to set the entity state to Detached.

P.S. In general, Use Scoped Lifetime for DbContext per UnitOfWork

It's generally best to keep a single DbContext instance per logical unit of work and avoid passing entities between different contexts or across service boundaries.

Q: Strikethrough code using Markdown on GitHub A:

After much much trying, I finally got it to work! It boils down to this:

  • inside ``` block, nothing is rendered (other than syntax highlights for language specified)
  • inside <code> block, markdown won't render, only HTML. You can use <strike>. It's fine, but you don't get the syntax coloring
  • now for the magic: use HTML for striking, and markdown for coloring:
<strike>

```language
  this is
  multiline code
```

</strike>

P.S. ``` blocks should always be surrounded by blank lines to work

Q: The result on test device is always 100 A:

Put the value where you divide by 100 in another variable and print the value to see what is going on.

let finalValue = round(ergebnis * 100) / 100.0
println("\(finalValue)")
ergebnisLabel.text = "\(finalValue)"

It looks like there may be an issue with dividing an int type by a floating point type, and doing it in the string literal is not able to convert to that value.

So you could also make sure the value you are dividing by 100.0 is a double if you want to do the calculation inline.

ergebnisLabel.text = "\(Double(round(ergebnis*100)) / 100.0)"
